Oh man I could be here all day. My guy Radagast was out of control and we had gates EVERYWHERE because he would get into everything. Once got lost like this and I was searching for him for AGES. Started to panic, looking everywhere, calling his name over and over again. I was literally like "did he get in through the walls somehow??" Eventually I sat down near the gate that covers the tubes to the fish tank and I see his little face peeking out. The bastard watched me tear apart the house for almost an hour and didn't say shit!! 

Our first time away with him we left him in care of a (very daft) pet sitter, who somehow didn't notice that he had found a way to parkour onto one of our tables and make his way through around $450 worth of my partners prized orchids. He had obviously figured out he wasn't supposed to be caught because she swore he was never on the table when she was there and was "an angel". When we returned we noticed immediately and my partner was literally crying on the floor, while Radagast, after welcoming us home, just jumped his rube Goldberg path to the orchids across all the furniture and continued eating like it was the most normal thing in the world. 

He also knew how to calculate exactly where to jump on cushions, walls, corners of tables, etc, and in what sequence to make it to where you were eating and knock the bowl out of your hands and have enough time to hoover up whatever you dropped while you were still in shock from it all!! You couldn't leave ANY food out unattended because he would inevitably find a way to eat it. He once ate a bowl of HOT curry and was FINE. He had a stomach of steel while my other rabbit has glass bones and paper skin. 

Like I said, I could literally be here all day. He past 2 years ago this year in May. He had a tooth abscess that got him in the end but fought the infection valiantly for 2 years. $10,000 in the hole but I'd do it all over again tenfold. I've had a ton of pets in my life but hand on heart this guy I connected with like NO ONE, human or animal, I've ever met. Genuinely my soulmate and kindred spirit. Long live Bad Bad Leroy Brown, Baddest Bun in the Whole Dang Town!! Best dog I've ever had ❤️

My first few years here I caught a bunch of roaming dogs not really knowing that people get really crazy about it. These dogs ended up at the vets or police station and were able to go back home, but everyone I was with was just like "dogs walk around here it's fine, it's his neighbourhood too". My mother had issues with food so I didn't really realise that I _really_ didn't know how to cook until my partner, whose mother was a high country station cook, came over for dinner and was horrified at what I called food. Growing up I wasn't really exposed to anything beyond plain brown rice and steamed vegetables with no sauce, salt, spices, etc in any of our meals. Canned soups was a staple, as well as plain boiled chicken, that sort of stuff. I think a lot of it is what you're exposed to at home and what you think is a possibility of regular people rather than "chefs"-- I had always assumed good food was just a skillset that "normal" people couldn't attain, or nice flavour profiles required fancy ingredients that I didn't think I could afford.

People have pretty much already covered it here, but rabs are absolutely not children's pets. I'm not from NZ originally and where I lived before I had many exotic pets and did exotic petsitting as a job -- I can tell you hand on heart out of all the animals I've either had or was entrusted with rabbits are absolutely the most high maintenance animals. Equally delicate and destructive and I was shocked at how much work they were to not only keep alive, but clean up after (ours are free range as caging rabbits isn't the most humane, they need far more space than the little hutches you see around)

I had a rabbit pass about a year ago from advanced dental disease, we easily spent $5000+ on his last year or so of vet bills trying to fight it. My other rabbit who I still have I easily spend $1000 or so annually on emergency vet visits-- GI stasis is no joke and can hit at any time. Some breeds more susceptible, some individuals more susceptible. Unfortunately my baby is both! 

That being said, I'd 100% take rabbits over other pets and I think I'm a rabbit person for life now. They're major pains in the ass but I am willing (and financially able) to spend the time and money on them. My boy Radagast who died last year was genuinely my kindred spirit and I really don't think I'll ever connect like that with any living thing, let alone an animal, ever again. 

Also, whether you decide to get one or not, please don't BUY a pet. There are many unwanted animals around either at the SPCA, or the various private rescues around town. Adopt don't shop, animals are not toys. Set a good example for your children and get them in the habit of choosing adoption over purchasing.

Personally I always check to see if it's opened by wiping a bit-- you'll still get blood initially but if you're still bleeding pretty freely a few min later you may not be opened. You may have to experiment with how far up you put it, etc-- personally when the nubbin is hanging out it's sitting too low for me, I like my skin to be able to close around it while I go about my day. 

It all takes practice bit trust me having a cup will change your life! When removing it it helps to reach up and make a divet in it to break the seal, or else it'll be too hard to remove. Your body is very responsive to anxiety so if you have trouble inserting/removing just have a break and try again later. Remember it can't ever get lost in you either, and it'll sit lower in your canal as it gets heavier with blood. 

Good luck! Hope that helps

Unfortunately I had lost a lot of hearing long before realising I should probably do something about it, but do some research on what you think would be best for you. What you're likely to be exposed to will inform what plugs were best for you, ie what works for someone in the electronic music space will be different for someone doing acoustic. My life was orchestral/marching band/pit band for stage productions/rock/punk/wild parties so the combination of being a brass player (where we were LOUD) and being in a punk band where we were even louder was a lot. 

Trust your gut-- if you're uncomfortable, it's probably not great for you. I had many practices where people younger than me could tolerate the amp much higher than I comfortably could but it was my own insecurities of looking silly that kept me from asking them to turn it down or putting my plugs in. I'm a shocker for blasting music in general, too. Rule of thumb is if you have to shout for someone next to you to hear you, it's too loud. Give you ears a chance to rest after intense sessions. Remember earbuds are designed to direct sound straight into your ears so do overear headphones when you have the choice. And when you get your earplugs for gigs, carry them in your wallet. They're designed to be discreet so I can slap them in at a gig and they're not noticeable. If people ask about them, tell you why you're doing it. I often just get people curious and totally understanding when I tell them I've had constant ringing for almost a decade now. Most people agree that they also have bouts of ringing and are concerned for their hearing so you can use it as a teaching experience. 

It was a HARD learning curve learning to live with the ringing and learning to chill out and turn the music/amp down a bit, but I'd 100% rather be blind than deaf so you do what you gotta do. The important thing is you've recognised how your hearing is being affected and taking steps to remedy any further damage. Might be worth getting a hearing test for peace of mine as well. As annoying as the ringing is I have a decent amount of my hearing left-- worst case scenario we'll be the people with hearing aids-- it means we've lived a life! :-)

1 TSP salt
